prize_parts.citation: For the discovery that liquid-liquid phase separation of multivalent biomolecules is a general principle by which living cells organize their interior

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged. The chemical discovery I would cite, in answer to Heiner Linke's question, is that weakly interacting multivalent macromolecules demix into dense and dilute liquid phases inside cells, so that classical phase equilibria, with concentration thresholds, tie-lines and interaction valency, set where and when cellular compartments exist without membranes. Brangwynne and Hyman showed this for P granules in 2009, and Rosen's work on multivalent signalling proteins gave the quantitative, reconstitutable physical-chemical framework. This is a new concept of molecular organisation, not a tool, and after about fifteen years it is independently reproduced and used to frame nucleoli, stress granules, transcription and aggregation disease. Nothing else on the shortlist represents physical chemistry as a discipline, and I do not accept that the shortlist should be judged only on synthesis, therapeutic reach or methods.
statement.case_against: Support is thin: after round 1 I am still the only member who prefers B061, and I should say plainly that no support count is a reason to prefer it. The strongest scientific objection is that physiological relevance is not settled. Many in vitro condensates may reflect overexpression, crowding or concentration artefacts, and showing that phase separation as such, rather than another assembly mechanism, is required for a function is hard. The credit is also split among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag, any three names leave out real contributions, and a Physiology or Medicine framing is plausible. I take Daniel Aili's and Heiner Linke's concern seriously that a prize should wait until functional necessity is demonstrated, and I cannot claim the debate is closed. I am keeping my position because the principle, as opposed to every individual condensate, is well supported by reconstitution and by quantitative phase-diagram measurements.

responses.point: Linke asked what exactly is the chemical discovery that would be cited for B061, and holds that base editing (B060) is a clear chemical principle that is easy to explain.
responses.response: The citation is the physical-chemical principle itself, liquid-liquid demixing of multivalent biomolecules as a cellular organising mechanism, which is why my wording now says so. I accept that B060 is easier to explain, and its Liu-lab attribution is the cleanest of the biological candidates. But I still see it as an engineering advance on a platform recognised in 2020, and the Target-AID attribution cost you and Chabes both name has not been answered in round 1. If the committee prefers a tool prize to a concept prize, that is a legitimate choice, but it should be made openly. I do not move to B060, and I am not ranking it below B012 because of any doubt about its mechanism.

responses.point: Aili is more cautious on B061 than I am, wants the question of whether condensates are functionally essential in vivo resolved before a prize, and builds B012 on induced proximity as a transferable design principle.
responses.response: I accept the criticism of B061, and it is the main thing that could still move me. The principle rests on reconstitution and phase-diagram work, while the in vivo necessity claim is still contested, and I cannot resolve that from the files. For that reason I now list B012 as my first alternative rather than B019. I agree with Aili that induced proximity is transferable chemistry. Where I differ is that the Crews and Deshaies PROTAC concept and Handa's cereblon work are separate lineages, and a single citation covering both makes the configuration weaker than it looks. No degrader is approved yet, and Ciulli's ternary-complex work is excluded from every B012 configuration proposed so far.

responses.point: Brzezinski supports B012 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa because the PROTAC concept and the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism share one molecular-recognition logic, and he accepts that Ciulli goes unrecognised.
responses.response: I respect that you state the Ciulli cost openly, and the shared ternary-complex logic is a real chemical unifier. As someone who works with interfaces and cooperativity, I would find the unified citation more convincing if the committee could say that the cooperative ternary complex is the achievement, because that is exactly what Ciulli's structural work established. A Crews, Deshaies, Handa trio rewards the concept and the target, while the structure-based design is left outside. Your answer to the chair's question about the third seat would decide whether B012 is one achievement or two for me. Until then I rank it behind B061 on conceptual novelty but ahead of the other candidates.

responses.point: Aqvist and Somfai both support Buchwald and Hartwig (B055) as the only shortlisted candidate with both clean attribution and unambiguous maturity, distinct from the 2010 prize.
responses.response: The two-name attribution and thirty years of use are real strengths, and I agree maturity is not a concern. The chair's question stands, namely what C-N coupling added conceptually beyond the Pd(0)/Pd(II) manifold recognised in 2010, and Somfai concedes he is working from memory on Kosugi. Overdue recognition and broad utility argue for importance. They do not show a new principle. I would not oppose B055 in a vote, but if the question is which candidate adds a new concept, I place B061 above it and B012 and B060 on the same level.

uncertainties: Whether functional necessity of condensates in vivo is established well enough that the principle can be treated as settled rather than as a hypothesis under test, which is the point on which I could move to B012.
Whether Rosen or the Pappu and Mittag pair is the right third name, and whether any three-name split of this field is defensible.
Whether the Chemistry framing for B061 holds against a Physiology or Medicine framing, since the founding observations were made in cell biology.
Whether B012 is one achievement or two lineages, and whether leaving out Ciulli is acceptable.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional tie to any credited candidate is apparent, so I see no recusal issue. I disclose scientific proximity: condensates touch the soft-matter and lipid-protein assembly work in my group, and B019 (ionizable lipid self-assembly) overlaps directly with my research area, which is one reason I treat it only as an alternative. Daniel Aili and I have overlapping interests in peptide and lipid self-assembly, and I have noted that for the committee to judge. I also sit on the committee with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, and that has not led me to adopt their positions.
